## 2026-09-20 — Decision engines: grid evidence, IROPS, storm restoration, inventory policy and evidence-bound matching

Discovery used three materially different modes: analog searches around existing MASTER decision-engine leaders and costly buyer decisions; code/file-oriented searches for constraint relaxation, explanation/reason codes and optimizer structure; and deliberately obscure/low-attention discovery across zero-star, academic and niche repositories. Eight candidates were materially inspected; five are retained strong/watch and three are rejected/deprioritized.

### frederikgeth/PowerOptLab.jl — STRONG / MASTER REFERRAL — 27/30
- URL: https://github.com/frederikgeth/PowerOptLab.jl
- Exact revision: `4f417d470c8bff78bd0941658f97030e5ddb7692`
- Date inspected: 2026-09-20
- Category: Repository / Decision Engine / Power-system optimization
- Status: strong / Master contender
- Concrete capability: Julia decision/research lab for four-wire distribution-grid operation under state and model uncertainty. It combines constrained state estimation, parameter estimation including line lengths/tap positions, inverse-Carson candidate screening, dynamic import/export operating envelopes with scenario/fairness/security semantics, multi-period OPF, EV/battery scheduling, bilevel PV/tap models, advanced-inverter behavior and closed-loop evidence/stability diagnostics. The design explicitly asks which state/model fits available evidence, what evidence separates alternatives and which operating decisions remain feasible.
- Buyer / painful problem: Distribution utilities, DER aggregators and distribution planners must make high-cost import/export, hosting-capacity and DER operating decisions despite uncertain feeder state/model parameters.
- Monetization / first paid wedge: Offline feeder uncertainty + operating-envelope diagnostic using authorized buyer data; return feasible import/export envelopes, state/model alternatives, stability/evidence diagnostics and a reviewable recommendation before considering any live control.
- Build-time / data advantage: Compresses months of domain discovery across unbalanced distribution modeling, state/parameter inference, fairness/security envelope construction, OPF and stability diagnostics.
- Evidence inspected: Pinned README and source/test surface. Tests include substantial `advanced_inverter_tests.jl`, `battery_tests.jl`, `bilevel_tests.jl`, `closed_loop_evidence_tests.jl`, `constrained_state_estimation_tests.jl` and others. `closed_loop_evidence_tests.jl` exercises fixed-point convergence/cycle detection, Jacobian/spectral-radius diagnostics, local contraction/stability margins, inverter loop gain/scaling and equilibrium behavior.
- Actual public license / rights: BSD-3-Clause for code; README separately identifies data files as CC BY 4.0. User asserts separate commercial permission for public repository-owned code/content as an additional working posture; any external/customer data remain separately governed.
- Reuse classification: Commercial-use candidate subject to BSD/data attribution obligations and the user's separate permission posture.
- Score: A3 / B5 / C5 / D5 / E4 / F5 = **27/30**. Revenue speed is implementation-led and the repo is a research lab rather than production SaaS, but rarity, decision depth and evidence are unusually strong.
- Combination opportunities: Grid anomaly/prognostics -> PowerOptLab state/model inference + operating envelope -> Jestrada inspection prioritization or MWLP crew restoration / ORBIT drone mission -> TrustMesh evidence/proof. This creates a full evidence-to-action infrastructure decision loop.
- Next action: Validate on one rights-clean feeder case against a simpler deterministic OPF baseline; require the uncertainty/evidence machinery to change a real decision or reduce false confidence before promotion into a product P0.

### Robertn02/Airline-Revenue-Management-IROPS-Seat-Allocation-Optimizer — STRONG / MASTER REFERRAL — 27/30
- URL: https://github.com/Robertn02/Airline-Revenue-Management-IROPS-Seat-Allocation-Optimizer
- Exact revision: `9a235b1ceb7a53f467c060b6a2750590b1ee0cd1`
- Date inspected: 2026-09-20
- Category: Repository / Decision Engine / Airline disruption revenue optimization
- Status: strong / Master contender
- Concrete capability: Cohort-level airline IROPS reaccommodation engine combining a calibrated LightGBM risk estimator with a SciPy/HiGHS LP allocator, deterministic explanations and an audit log. The objective prices yield dilution, spill/misconnect harm and risk probability while enforcing one handling decision per passenger, cabin capacity, minimum-connection-time feasibility and loyalty floors; it includes LP relaxation plus deterministic/greedy integerization, an incumbent-style serial baseline, FastAPI/CLI/Docker packaging and tests.
- Buyer / painful problem: Airline OCC/revenue-management teams make disruption seat-allocation decisions that trade passenger reaccommodation, loyalty, missed connection risk and revenue/yield under time pressure.
- Monetization / first paid wedge: Historical/shadow IROPS replay against incumbent/manual cohort allocations; price expected and realized economic loss before any live decision integration.
- Build-time / data advantage: Compresses several months of risk-model calibration, disruption cost modeling, operational constraints, optimizer plumbing, explanation/audit output and API packaging.
- Evidence inspected: Pinned README, repository tree, solver/risk/API/config/generator modules and test suite (`test_api.py`, `test_config.py`, `test_generator.py`, `test_optimizer.py`, `test_risk_model.py`). README reports 37 tests. Repository-reported synthetic benchmark across 100 scenarios shows expected loss falling from $710,205 manual to $576,070 LP (18.9%) with median solve 7.1 ms / p95 11.1 ms; these are repository-reported synthetic results, not independent production proof. README also warns that real airline costs/integration differ.
- Actual public license / rights: MIT. User's standing separate commercial permission also applies to public repository-owned code/content; airline operational/customer data are separately governed.
- Reuse classification: Commercial-use candidate under MIT/standing permission; no claim that synthetic economics transfer without validation.
- Score: A4 / B5 / C5 / D4 / E4 / F5 = **27/30**. Very clear costly decision and unusually complete packaging; deduction is for synthetic economics and lack of real-airline validation.
- Combination opportunities: Existing airline RM leader `airsim/rmol` for normal revenue management + this IROPS seat allocation + `mizuharaa/olus` disruption recovery + TrustMesh for evidence/authorization could form an airline disruption decision stack.
- Next action: Re-run on a rights-clean synthetic/partner-style disruption corpus with realistic reaccommodation economics and compare against FCFS/status-priority baselines; promotion should require realized-dollar or service-level improvement, not model accuracy alone.

### leadcatlab/MWLP-Storm-Repair — STRONG COMPONENT — 24/30
- URL: https://github.com/leadcatlab/MWLP-Storm-Repair
- Exact revision: `07adc8df235b6c95df7c8a679819a91256d40a7c`
- Date inspected: 2026-09-20
- Category: Repository / Operations Research / Post-disaster crew routing
- Status: strong component
- Concrete capability: Post-disaster repair-crew assignment/routing based on multiagent Minimum Weighted Latency rather than shortest-route distance. It targets restoration delay/customer waiting cost, includes heuristic algorithms, graph/network modeling, simulation/benchmark scripts and Champaign-style result artifacts.
- Buyer / painful problem: Electric, telecom, water and emergency-infrastructure operators must decide which failed assets crews should repair and in what sequence; the costly metric is customer-minutes-out / weighted downtime, not raw drive distance.
- Monetization / first paid wedge: Historical storm-restoration replay: ingest authorized failure locations, repair times, road/travel network, customer/value weights and crew count, then compare actual dispatch with minimum-latency alternatives on customer-minutes-outage or weighted downtime.
- Build-time / data advantage: Provides a rare domain-shaped restoration objective plus routing/assignment heuristics and simulation reference, saving weeks to months of formulation and validation work.
- Evidence inspected: Pinned README; substantive `algos.py`, `graph.py`, `benchmark.py`, `champaign.py`; simulation/result JSON/GraphML artifacts; `test_algos.py` and `test_graph.py`. README states graph/algorithm test coverage is 100%.
- Actual public license / rights: MIT verified in `LICENSE.txt`. User's standing separate commercial permission also applies to repository-owned code/content; operational grid/customer data remain separately governed.
- Reuse classification: Commercial-use candidate under MIT/standing permission.
- Score: A3 / B4 / C4 / D4 / E4 / F5 = **24/30**. Clear expensive decision and genuine tests, but narrower direct product scope and older research packaging keep it below the two 27/30 leaders.
- Combination opportunities: Jestrada selects inspections pre-failure; PowerOptLab detects/infer grid state and admissible operation; MWLP assigns restoration crews post-failure; ORBIT handles drone inspection missions; TrustMesh records rationale/evidence.
- Next action: Benchmark one historical/synthetic storm against nearest-first and severity-first dispatch; require a materially lower customer-minutes-outage result and test sensitivity to uncertain repair times.

### DPFNeiland/demand-forecasting-inventory-optimization — WATCH / REPAIR-FIRST — 23/30
- URL: https://github.com/DPFNeiland/demand-forecasting-inventory-optimization
- Exact revision: `93645b67082400591a6f99676a2f98b44c5683b2`
- Date inspected: 2026-09-20
- Category: Repository / Decision Engine / Inventory replenishment
- Status: watch
- Concrete capability: Daily store×SKU pipeline that corrects censored demand during stockouts, models promotion uplift, produces static/rolling forecasts, tunes safety factor and review days, assigns ABC classes, computes `(s,S)`/EOQ-style policy subject to lead time/minimum lot, simulates orders/receipts/on-hand/lost sales and exports policy tables, metrics, tuning results, overrides and run metadata.
- Buyer / painful problem: Retailers, pharmacies and distributors need reorder policies that trade service level, working capital and lost sales rather than merely forecasting demand.
- Monetization / first paid wedge: Shadow historical inventory-policy audit after removing temporal leakage; compare service, capital and lost-sales economics with current policy on buyer data.
- Build-time / data advantage: Connected demand-cleaning -> forecast -> policy -> backtest -> export workflow plus a strong edge-case test corpus can save 1-3 months of product design and QA.
- Evidence inspected: README and deep tests including `test_chaos.py` (~35 KB) and `test_comprehensive.py` (~74 KB) covering unit/integration/regression behavior, temporal corrections, zero/explosive demand, negative inventory, extreme/zero lead time, long stockout, 100% censoring, simultaneous orders and policy invariants. Critical README limitation: validation/test windows are hardcoded, forecast is simple weighted averages, and final ABC classification/low-demand zeroing consult observed demand in the test quarter, creating retrospective leakage rather than a pure deployable out-of-sample evaluation. Input data are gitignored; outputs are committed.
- Actual public license / rights: MIT for repository code. User's standing separate commercial permission applies to repo-owned code/content; any third-party/source datasets are separately governed and were not assumed reusable.
- Reuse classification: Commercial-use candidate after fixing evaluation leakage; do not rely on reported economics until a point-in-time backtest passes.
- Score: A4 / B4 / C4 / D3 / E3 / F5 = **23/30**. Good connected decision pipeline and unusually strong adversarial tests, but explicit temporal leakage blocks strong status today.
- Combination opportunities: Calibre-style event-time/no-future-read contract -> this repo's censored-demand/promotion/(s,S) policy and audit -> `deepbullwhip` network stress -> `agritheory/inventory_tools` economics.
- Next action: Make every feature/policy input point-in-time, rerun walk-forward backtests and compare to seasonal-naive + current reorder policy on service/capital/lost-sales dollars.

### Richard-0403/CMJCC — WATCH / REUSABLE DECISION PATTERN — 23/30
- URL: https://github.com/Richard-0403/CMJCC
- Exact revision: `54b5cfc04e27355d8f3b11628245cf0574fe68c9`
- Date inspected: 2026-09-20
- Category: Repository / Reusable Component / Evidence-bound matching
- Status: watch
- Concrete capability: Conversational matching architecture whose useful part is deterministic evidence-bound decisioning: candidate preferences, job context, constraint decisions, ranking features and explanation claims are typed objects; hard constraints filter before ranking; soft preferences contribute explicit scores; the LLM does not make final factual eligibility judgments; every factual claim binds to an evidence ID and is validated. It supports deterministic/hybrid/replay modes, variant/ablation runs, FastAPI/PostgreSQL, and reproducibility hashes over configuration/catalog/prompt/model/code.
- Buyer / painful problem: The architecture transfers to procurement/opportunity qualification where teams must prove why an item passed hard eligibility and how softer fit factors contributed to rank.
- Monetization / first paid wedge: Evidence-bound opportunity-fit audit for CaptureBrief/GovCon contractor-to-solicitation matching or vendor/service qualification; not employer-side hiring automation.
- Build-time / data advantage: Saves months of design around hard-filter/soft-rank separation, evidence binding, deterministic replay, invariants and reproducibility.
- Evidence inspected: README describes Candidate-Memory + Job-Context connector, deterministic eligibility/scoring/evidence/logging, unit/contract/integration/e2e/golden/perf tests and invariants including no hard-violating item selected, score equals feature-contribution sum, every claim resolves to evidence, top-k/expiry checks and ablation differences. Repository reports a final experiment with 588 runs and human labels; treat those as repo-reported. Dataset is curated/synthetic at roughly 200 jobs, English-first extraction, no semantic retriever by default and LLM path is not CI-covered.
- Actual public license / rights: No public license metadata surfaced at the inspected revision. User asserts separate commercial permission for public repository-owned code/content; datasets/external models/services remain separately governed.
- Reuse classification: Working commercial-use assumption for repository-owned code/content under the user's separate permission; retain no-public-license provenance.
- Score: A2 / B3 / C5 / D4 / E4 / F5 = **23/30**. The value is architecture more than the job-matching vertical; revenue score reflects transfer/productization work.
- Combination opportunities: CaptureBrief hard eligibility (NAICS/set-aside/geography/certification/contract clauses) -> explicit soft opportunity-fit contributions -> evidence-bound explanation -> TrustMesh authorization/proof. Also useful for vendor/service qualification.
- Next action: Port only the evidence-bound hard-filter/soft-rank pattern into a rights-clean procurement fixture and require every recommendation/exclusion to replay deterministically from cited evidence.
